claim: Map which domains AI answers cite for 5 core queries (about 250 citations plus about 30 search results each), then target the most-cited sites, such as Healthline, for inclusion.
body: Being recommended in ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini or Google's AI answers depends heavily on the pages those systems retrieve and cite, so the speaker treats the citation list as the work plan. Method: choose five core buying queries for the cluster; for each, record the traditional results across search engines (about 30 per query) and the sources cited in AI answers (about 50 per query in his example, around 250 total); export, deduplicate and count how often each domain and page appears. For creatine, Healthline was the most cited domain on almost every query, followed by Reddit, Amazon, Forbes and specialist review sites. Then work the list from the top: ask to be included in the most-visible listicles, offer product for review, pay for sponsored placements where allowed, and sell on Amazon if the category's answers cite Amazon listings. He estimates that winning coverage on even 20 percent of the top ten cited domains moves visibility noticeably while competition is still thin. How to apply: repeat the same query set monthly and track your share of citations as the AEO metric.
conditions: Product categories where AI assistants answer buying questions with cited sources; brands able to fund outreach, samples or sponsorships.
fails_when: Categories where AI answers cite few third-party pages; health and finance niches where sponsored inclusion must be disclosed and some publishers refuse; citation sets change often, so a one-off map goes stale.

claim: Review and FAQ widgets that load by JavaScript after page load are invisible to most AI crawlers; disable JavaScript and reload to see what they read.
body: Most AI crawlers read only the HTML present when the page is first served; they do not run scripts. Many Shopify apps for reviews and FAQs insert their content with JavaScript after load, leaving only an empty placeholder in the HTML, so the reviews and answers that would help an assistant recommend your product never reach it. The source names Google's Gemini as the main exception. Checks: 1) open the product page with JavaScript disabled in the browser and reload; whatever disappears is invisible to those crawlers; 2) run a request with an AI crawler's user agent (for example curl with -A ClaudeBot) to confirm the page is reachable and not blocked; 3) read robots.txt to confirm common AI agents are allowed (Shopify generates it automatically unless edited); 4) validate product schema with a schema validator. Fixes: pick review and FAQ apps that render server-side or inject into the HTML, or put key FAQs in the theme template. Practitioner guidance; crawler behaviour changes, so recheck periodically.
conditions: Stores relying on app widgets for reviews, FAQs or specifications and wanting to be cited by AI assistants.
fails_when: Crawlers that render JavaScript (the source names Gemini); apps that already server-render content; robots.txt deliberately blocking AI agents by choice.

claim: Shopify's global product catalog feeds AI shopping tools from back-end data only; eligibility needs the agentic storefront on and products with a title, an image and a non-zero price.
body: Besides crawling your public pages, AI assistants and third-party shopping apps can read Shopify's global product catalog, compiled from every eligible store. Developers are already building niche AI search tools on it (the source shows apps for finding specific LEGO bricks and Tesla parts across Shopify stores). To be included, the store needs the agentic storefront setting enabled, and products must meet basic requirements such as a title, at least one image and a price above zero, plus Shopify's terms. You can ask Sidekick whether the store is eligible. Because the catalog is built only from back-end data, it sees the title, description, variants and metafields, not your theme. So: 1) write descriptions with concrete attributes (material, size, colour, use case); 2) clean up metafields, since the source saw stale metafields from uninstalled apps such as old review apps flowing into the catalog; 3) keep prices and stock accurate. Practitioner summary of a new and changing feature; confirm current requirements in Shopify's documentation.

body: According to this 2026 tutorial, Google added a control that removes a site's content from AI Overviews and AI Mode while leaving its standard search rankings unchanged. It started with site owners in the UK and was described as rolling out globally. The speaker advises against using it for most businesses: being the source an AI answer quotes is usually better than being invisible in it, and a lost click may not matter if the brand still wins the sale. The decision method: open the generative AI performance report first, see how many AI impressions each page earns, and weigh that against any clicks you believe the AI features are taking. Opting out mainly makes sense for content whose value depends on the visit itself, such as ad-supported or gated content, which is rarely the case for a store. Treat the existence and exact behaviour of the toggle as a practitioner report and confirm the current rules in Google Search Central documentation, which is tier 1 and wins on mechanics, before switching anything.

claim: When a page holds its Google position but loses clicks, check CTR against position, then Search Console's 2026 generative AI report for heavy AI Overview impressions on that page.
body: A common pattern since about 2024 is steady rankings with falling clicks. The tutorial's diagnosis: first compare click-through rate against position over time. If a page sits at position three but its CTR has shrunk for months, either the title and description went stale against a better competitor snippet (rewrite the snippet), or Google put something above the result that answers the query, most often an AI Overview. Per the speaker, Google released a generative AI performance report in Search Console in June 2026, in beta and not yet on every property. It shows impressions, meaning how often a link to your site appeared inside AI Overviews or AI Mode, split by page, country and device. It has no click or position data yet. If the pages losing clicks show heavy AI impressions, the content is being read inside the answer rather than lost in ranking. Next step: sort the report by impressions to find pages the AI already uses, note their structure (direct, clearly structured answers to buyer questions), and produce more pages in that form. The report covers only Google's own AI features, not ChatGPT, Gemini app, Perplexity or Claude. Practitioner description of a beta feature; confirm in your own property.

fails_when: The report is not yet on the property; the click loss coincides with a ranking or demand drop (seasonality, algorithm update), which needs the comparison-by-page method instead; queries where Google shows no AI feature.

claim: Branded web mentions correlate most with AI Overview visibility (0.664 across 75,000 brands), YouTube mentions with ChatGPT (0.737), and listicles are 43.8% of cited pages: earn third-party lists.
body: AI engines recommend brands that many independent sources agree on, so the work shifts from ranking one page to being named in many places. In Ahrefs' study of 75,000 brands, the number of branded web mentions had the strongest correlation with appearing in Google AI Overviews (0.664), stronger than backlinks, referring domains or domain rating. YouTube mentions correlated 0.737 with ChatGPT visibility, and YouTube is about 5.6 percent of all AI Overview citations. Across AI Overviews and ChatGPT, 43.8 percent of cited pages were listicles or comparison pages. How to apply for a store: (1) find 'best', 'top', 'versus' and 'alternative' prompts where competitors are named and you are not; (2) list the editorial roundups and comparison pages those answers cite and pitch them with samples, data or affiliate terms; (3) seed honest discussion where buyers talk (Reddit, niche forums) without astroturfing; (4) publish YouTube videos targeting search queries in your category rather than chasing viral views, since transcripts are indexed and cited; (5) keep your own comparison and FAQ pages current as a third tier. These are correlations, not proof that adding mentions causes visibility.
conditions: Brands in categories with active 'best of' coverage and buyer discussion; Ahrefs datasets as of late 2025.
fails_when: Very new or tiny categories with no editorial lists to get into; paid or fake mentions and Reddit astroturfing can backfire on reputation and platform bans; correlation may reflect that already-popular brands get both mentions and citations.

claim: Check default CDN bot settings are not blocking AI crawlers (5.9% of 140M sites block GPTBot) and redirect AI-referred 404s; assistants send 2.87x more 404 visits.
body: Two technical leaks quietly cut AI visibility and waste AI-referred visitors. First, access: Ahrefs found about 5.9 percent of 140 million websites block OpenAI's GPTBot, often by accident, for example through a CDN or bot-management setting that blocks AI crawlers by default (the course names Cloudflare's AI bot setting). Check robots.txt and your CDN or WAF rules, and decide deliberately which agents to allow: AI search and citation crawlers are distribution, while scrapers and training-only bots may be blocked. Also make sure key content is in server-rendered HTML, since many AI crawlers do not execute JavaScript. Second, broken landings: AI assistants send visitors to 404 pages 2.87 times more often than Google Search, and about 1 percent of URLs clicked from ChatGPT return 404, because models guess or misremember URLs. Steps: in analytics, filter sessions from AI referrers that hit 404 status; group the requested URLs; 301-redirect each to the closest real product, collection or guide; and make the 404 page itself useful with search and best sellers.
conditions: Stores on CDNs or bot-management products (Cloudflare, Shopify's edge, WAFs) and any site receiving AI referral traffic; data from Ahrefs as of 2025.
fails_when: Brands that deliberately opt out of AI training or have licensing reasons to block some crawlers; blocking training bots while allowing search and user-triggered agents is a valid split, so allowlisting everything is not the goal.

claim: For AI citations length barely matters (0.04 correlation; 53.4% of cited pages under 1,000 words) but freshness does: cited content is about 25.7% fresher than organic results.
body: Ahrefs analysed over 174,000 pages cited in AI Overviews and found almost no relationship between word count and being cited (correlation 0.04); 53.4 percent of cited pages were under 1,000 words. Recency mattered more: AI-cited content was on average 25.7 percent fresher than pages ranking in classic results, 89.7 percent of ChatGPT's top-cited pages had been updated in 2025, and 76 percent had been refreshed within the previous 30 days. The practical implication for a store's guides, comparison pages and FAQs: stop padding pages for length, and instead (1) put the direct answer first in each section (bottom line up front), since retrieval pulls chunks rather than whole pages; (2) make every H2 section understandable on its own, with the product or brand named rather than referred to as 'it'; (3) keep a refresh calendar for the 5 to 10 pages that matter most, making substantive updates (new prices, specs, current-year comparisons) rather than date changes; (4) refresh older pages that still rank or used to get traffic before writing new ones. A page untouched for six months is at a disadvantage for AI citation.
conditions: Informational, comparison and FAQ content intended to be cited by AI Overviews and ChatGPT; Ahrefs data from 2025.
fails_when: Freshness signals faked by changing dates without content changes are unlikely to help; and topics that are genuinely static (care instructions, sizing basics) gain less from refreshes than fast-moving comparisons.

body: Most AI influence never shows up as a referral. Across platforms only about 28 percent of AI mentions include a link: roughly 51.6 percent on Perplexity, 36.8 percent in AI Mode, 26.9 percent in ChatGPT and 10.7 percent in AI Overviews. A shopper who sees your brand named, then types your URL or searches your name, lands as direct or branded organic traffic. Ahrefs therefore measures with three inputs used together: (1) AI referral traffic, via a custom GA4 channel grouping that matches AI referrer domains with a regex (chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai, gemini, copilot and similar); on average this is only about 0.25 percent of a site's traffic, and Google still sends about 210 times more than the top AI platforms combined; (2) AI crawler and citation-bot hits in server logs, showing which pages AI systems fetch; (3) self-reported attribution, adding options such as 'AI assistant (ChatGPT, Perplexity)' and 'Google AI Overview' to a post-purchase or checkout 'how did you hear about us' question. claim: Publish an official brand-facts FAQ: in an Ahrefs test Gemini and Perplexity repeated planted fake sources in 37-39% of answers; ChatGPT cited the official FAQ 84%.
body: AI engines fill gaps in what they know about a brand with whatever sources they find, accurate or not. Ahrefs created a fictional luxury brand, planted three contradictory sources about it on a blog, Reddit and Medium, then asked eight AI platforms about it. Gemini and Perplexity repeated the invented details (fake founders, cities, pricing stories) in 37 to 39 percent of answers, presented as fact. ChatGPT stayed under 7 percent and cited the brand's official FAQ in 84 percent of its answers. The lesson for a store is to leave no factual gap for others to fill: publish one crawlable official page answering who founded the brand, where it is based and ships from, how products are made and sourced, price ranges, materials, warranty, returns and what the brand does not sell, with each answer stated plainly and kept current. Then run your brand-name prompts monthly on each platform, note any wrong claims and their cited sources, and correct those sources where you can (reviews of outdated info, old press, marketplace listings). Treat sentiment and accuracy as a tracked metric alongside mention count.
conditions: Any brand, especially newer or smaller ones with thin third-party coverage, or brands that have changed pricing, ownership or product lines.
fails_when: Large established brands with abundant consistent coverage are less exposed; and a single experiment on one fictional brand does not give stable per-platform rates, so treat the percentages as illustrative.

claim: Track AI visibility per platform: only 7 of the top 50 cited domains overlap across AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity, and over 45% of citations churn every two days.
body: AI answer engines retrieve from different sources, so one visibility number hides most of the picture. Ahrefs found only 7 of the 50 most-cited domains appeared on all three of Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity (14 percent overlap). Perplexity tracks Google rankings most closely, with about 28.6 percent of its citations from Google top-10 pages; ChatGPT overlaps only 8 to 10 percent and leans on high-authority publishers (median domain rating of its top-cited pages about 90). AI Overviews once drew 76 percent of citations from the top 10, but a later study puts it nearer 38 percent as YouTube and Reddit grow; AI Overviews and AI Mode give 86 percent semantically similar answers yet share only 13.7 percent of citations. AI Overviews appear on about 21 percent of keywords overall, 58 percent of question queries and 46 percent of queries of seven or more words. Over 45 percent of AI Overview citations change at each refresh, roughly every two days. How to apply: build a fixed panel of buyer prompts (best, top, versus, review, alternative), run it on each platform on a schedule, record mentions and citations per platform, and judge trends over weeks, not single checks.
conditions: Brands measuring or working on AI search visibility, particularly categories where buyers ask comparison and 'best X' questions; figures from Ahrefs datasets as of late 2025.
fails_when: Platform behaviour shifts quickly; these shares will move with model and product changes, so re-measure rather than reuse the numbers after about six months.

claim: A single wire press release (about $80, about $6 each in bulk) can be syndicated widely enough to be cited in Google AI Overviews and ChatGPT for its headline phrase.
body: Low-cost newswire services syndicate releases to many news and finance sites, which assistants and AI Overviews treat as sources. Examples from the episode: an SEO author bought a single release (about $80; bulk plans bring the price to about $6 per release) with the phrase 'best-selling SEO book' in the title, subheading and first sentence, and the release then ranked first on Google and was cited by AI Overviews and ChatGPT for that phrase. The guest separately ran a test with a fictitious company and a claimed near-five-star rating, and assistants repeated it confidently, which shows both the power and the misinformation risk. Legitimate uses for a store: product launches, sponsorships and community activity, awards, and correcting an outdated narrative; repeat the exact phrase you want associated with the brand in the headline and opening line. claim: Prompt trackers on free ChatGPT often record answers given without any web search, so no citations appear; compare logged-in and logged-out runs, repeat prompts, and discount answers lacking search.
body: AI visibility tools usually run your prompts and screenshot the answer. The guest found much of his tracked data useless because the free version of ChatGPT frequently answered from model memory without searching the web, so no sources were cited and the answer reflected old training data (it named a former prime minister as current a year after he left office). Answers also vary between runs, between logged-in paid accounts and logged-out sessions, and with small changes in wording. How to measure more reliably: for each important prompt, run it several times, in a logged-out session and a logged-in or paid account, and with a few phrasings; record whether a web search happened, which sources were cited and whether the brand was mentioned; only compare citation share across runs that searched. Treat no-search answers as a separate signal about what the model already believes, which changes only with training updates. Report AI visibility as a range over repeated runs, not a single screenshot.

claim: Read the sub-searches (fan-out queries) ChatGPT runs for your prompts and use that wording in page titles, URLs, H1s and first sentences, including best-X-for-Y category pages.
body: When an assistant searches, it rewrites the prompt into one or more web queries, often adding qualifiers such as the year, use cases or review sites. Perplexity shows these openly. For ChatGPT, the host's method: run a prompt that triggers a search, open the browser developer tools network tab, filter by the conversation ID from the URL, refresh, open the matching response and search it for 'queries' to see the exact searches. Repeat across prompts to learn the phrasing the model uses, then target that language on pages that can rank: page title, URL slug, H1 and the opening sentence. They observed ChatGPT adding a review site (G2) and well-known brand names into fan-out queries, so being present on the review and affiliate sites it searches matters too. For ecommerce, they note Google increasingly ranks category and product pages for best-of queries, so a category page titled like 'best fragrances for men' with the product grid can win bottom-funnel searches without a separate listicle. Prefer specific, high-intent use-case pages over top-of-funnel explainers that AI answers itself.

claim: Repeating one corrected fact across your site, founder videos, social posts and third-party articles shifted what ChatGPT said without search, from 9+ months to about 6, over two years.
body: Models answer some questions from training data without searching, so outdated or negative claims (often from old reviews) persist. The guest's case: a software company's model-stated implementation time was 9 to 12 months or more, traced to five-year-old G2 review wording. The fix was distribution of one consistent statement: the website stated implementation can take as little as three weeks; the founder posted myth-busting videos on Instagram and YouTube; third-party articles carried the same point. About two years later, the latest model without web search said about six months: not the target, but a measurable shift. A content capsule is a heading phrased as the buyer's question followed immediately by a short answer that makes sense on its own, so it can be lifted without the surrounding text. Rules from the presenter: (1) phrase H2s as the questions buyers and AI fan-out queries ask (how much does X cost, do I need Y, which size for Z); (2) answer in the first 20 to 25 words with the specific fact or range, never a warm-up line ('in the ever-evolving world of...'); going to 50 words is fine if still direct; (3) apply this to roughly 60 to 70 percent of the article and use the rest for process, examples and first-hand experience, which AI cannot copy from elsewhere; (4) keep links out of the capsule sentence itself but link every statistic or price claim to its source elsewhere in the section; (5) make each section readable out of context by naming the product rather than writing 'it'. For a store, the natural homes are buying guides, size and fit guides, care pages and product FAQs, where questions like 'which size for a 12 kg dog' have one clear answer.

body: Graphite tested whether purely AI-generated content (no human in the loop) wins in search and answers. Method: put thousands of searches into Google and questions into ChatGPT, collected the ranking URLs and citations, and scored them with an AI-content detector. They validated the detector on thousands of articles they generated and on a random 100,000-URL Common Crawl sample from before ChatGPT launched, where the false positive rate was about 8%. Result: around 10 to 12% of content in Google results and ChatGPT citations was AI-generated and about 90% was not, while their Common Crawl trend showed AI-generated pages now outnumber human-written ones on the web, so AI pages are heavily under-represented in what ranks. The guest's reasoning: if mass AI content worked, everyone would publish it and engines would end up summarising their own output, so they will act against it as Google did against scraped comparison pages around 2007. A second test feeding AI derivatives back into retrieval collapsed diverse opinions into one. How to apply: use AI for drafts and research, but have people add original data, expertise and editing, and spend budget on the few pages that matter.
conditions: Stores producing blog, guide or collection content at scale for search and answer engines.
fails_when: Detector-based studies carry error (about 8% false positives); engines' tolerance could change; heavily edited AI-assisted content is not what the study measured.
numbers: about 10 to 12% of ranking or cited content AI-generated, about 90% human
detector false positive rate about 8%
100,000-URL Common Crawl sample

topics: source corroboration and third party mentions
claim: In answer engines the 'head' is won by being mentioned in as many cited sources as possible, not by ranking one URL first, so new brands can win quickly.
body: Ethan Smith's distinction: on Google, the first blue link for 'best website builder' wins most clicks; in an LLM answer the model summarises many citations, and the brand mentioned most often across them tends to be named first. Because a citation can appear the day after a Reddit thread, YouTube video or blog mention, early-stage brands without domain authority can show up in answers quickly, whereas classic SEO usually pays off only later. He reports Webflow saw LLM visitors convert about 6x better than Google search visitors, and LLMs supplying about 8% of Webflow sign-ups. How to apply: 1) For each target prompt, list the cited sources by type: your site, YouTube or Vimeo, Reddit and Quora, tier-one affiliate publishers (Dotdash Meredith titles such as Good Housekeeping), smaller blogs. 2) Run a separate plan per type: standard SEO pages for your site; videos for specific, unglamorous high-value questions few creators cover; honest Reddit answers from named employees; paid or earned affiliate placements. 3) For commerce, answers now include shoppable product cards showing several sellers, so product schema and review counts matter and last-click referral traffic is a usable measure.
conditions: Brands in categories where shoppers ask assistants 'what is the best X'; especially newer brands without search authority.
fails_when: Categories where answers cite mostly marketplaces or one dominant publisher; paid affiliate mentions without disclosure breach FTC rules; the 6x conversion figure is one B2B SaaS client and may not hold for impulse products.
numbers: Webflow: LLM traffic converts about 6x Google search traffic
LLMs about 8% of Webflow sign-ups
average chat prompt about 25 words versus about 6 for a Google search (as cited by the guest)

claim: Test AEO tactics with a control group: about 200 tracked questions, 100 left untouched and 100 given the intervention, compared over a few weeks before and after.
body: Smith's point is that answer visibility drifts on its own (answers vary per run and overall LLM usage is rising), so a before-and-after chart without a control misleads, and most published AEO best practices have never been tested. Method: 1) Build a question set from your search and paid-search terms and competitors' paid terms, converted into natural questions, plus questions from sales calls, support tickets and Reddit. 2) Load them into an answer tracker (he says around 60 exist and are largely interchangeable, so pick the cheapest that does what you need). 3) Track for a couple of weeks to get a baseline share of voice: how often you appear across repeated runs and phrasings, and your average position. 4) Split about 200 questions into 100 control (no action) and 100 test; optionally break the test group into buckets by tactic (Reddit comments, a YouTube video, a paid affiliate mention). 5) Act on the test group only, track a couple of weeks more, and keep tactics that rose while the control did not. 6) Repeat the test before treating a tactic as proven, since one-off results in search often turn out to be coincidence.
conditions: Brands with enough relevant prompts (around 200) to split into groups and an answer-tracking tool; any category.
fails_when: Very narrow categories without enough distinct prompts to form comparable groups; tactics that spill over (a brand-wide PR mention lifts control prompts too) blur the comparison.
numbers: about 200 questions: 100 control, 100 test
a couple of weeks baseline and a couple of weeks after
about 60 answer-tracking tools on the market

claim: Google says AI Overviews and AI Mode need no special files, AI text files, markup or schema.
body: A page must simply be indexed and eligible to show with a snippet, and its traffic is counted in Search Console's Web performance data. Google Search Central states there are no additional requirements or special optimisations to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode, and that site owners do not need new machine-readable files, AI text files or special schema.org markup. To be shown as a supporting link a page must be indexed and eligible to appear in Search with a snippet. Google recommends the usual basics: allow crawling in robots.txt, keep important content available as text, and make structured data match the visible text. Traffic from these features is included in the Search Console Performance report under the Web search type, not in a separate report. To limit what is shown, Google points to nosnippet, data-nosnippet, max-snippet and noindex; Google-Extended limits AI training and grounding in some other Google systems. How to apply: spend AI-search effort on indexable, text-first pages and accurate markup, not on files such as llms.txt sold as a Google requirement.
conditions: Google Search AI Overviews and AI Mode.
fails_when: Other assistants (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Copilot) have their own crawlers and rules; Google may change these features.
numbers: No special files, markup or schema required
Must be indexed and snippet-eligible

claim: OpenAI runs separate crawlers: OAI-SearchBot decides whether a site can appear in ChatGPT search answers, GPTBot gathers training data, and ChatGPT-User fetches pages for user actions; each robots.txt setting is independent and changes take about 24 hours.
body: OpenAI's crawler documentation says OAI-SearchBot is used to surface websites in ChatGPT's search features, and sites that opt out of it will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers. GPTBot crawls content that may be used to train generative AI models; disallowing it signals the content should not be used for training. ChatGPT-User handles certain user-initiated actions and is not used for automatic crawling. Each setting is independent of the others, and it can take about 24 hours after a robots.txt update for OpenAI's systems to adjust. How to apply: a store that wants to be recommended in ChatGPT must allow OAI-SearchBot; it may still choose to block GPTBot for training without losing search visibility.
conditions: Stores that want to appear in ChatGPT search answers.
fails_when: CDN or firewall bot rules can block a crawler even when robots.txt allows it; other assistants use their own crawler names.
numbers: About 24 hours for robots.txt changes to apply

claim: Shopify's agentic storefronts let buyers find and buy a store's products inside AI channels (ChatGPT, Google AI Mode and Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Meta).
body: It is on by default for eligible stores and needs Shopify Catalog eligibility plus completed terms, privacy and refund policies. Shopify's help centre describes agentic storefronts as letting customers discover and purchase products in AI channels, with Shop Pay available through personal AI agents. Channels named are ChatGPT, Google AI Mode and Gemini, Microsoft Copilot and Meta surfaces. Every channel needs the products to be eligible for Shopify Catalog, and the store must complete its Terms of service, Privacy policy and Return and refund policy in Settings, Policies. Each channel has its own rules, such as countries served, and eligibility is reviewed over time. Product data reaches the channels through Shopify Catalog, or for Google AI Mode and Gemini through the Google and YouTube channel or Merchant Center. It is active by default for eligible stores and managed under Sales channels, Agentic. How to apply: complete the three policy pages, fix product data that blocks catalog eligibility, and check which channels are on before relying on them.
conditions: Shopify stores in markets where these AI channels are offered.
fails_when: Non-Shopify stores; channel lists, countries and settings are changing quickly, so recheck the help page before each audit.
